# ADR-007: Data-class consistency and evidence-based recovery

Status: accepted educational architecture. Stage: 7. Date: 2026-11-02. Supersedes: none; preserve security and execution semantics from ADR-001–006.

## Situation and Alternatives

A saved answer may be absent on a lagging read copy; lost responses invite duplicate attempts, and authority outages invite unsafe stale permission. Compare primary-only reads, minimum-version eligible projections, stale-authority fallback and blind retry/failover. Choose current authoritative policy/budget/ownership decisions, eligible history projection reads with primary fallback, and no stale authorisation or uncertain-provider replay.

## Decision

Keep result persistence and outbox intent atomic locally. Deliver asynchronously with duplicate-safe transactional projection updates and a contiguous applied watermark. Reuse a stable scoped operation key after a lost acknowledgement; absence of a result after an external attempt still requires uncertainty handling. Carry remaining deadlines, bounded retry/probe policies, telemetry correlation and per-boundary recovery runbooks.

Real replication/failover must specify writer fencing, acknowledgement durability, RPO/RTO, minimum-version reads and restore/promotion tests. Quorum counts alone are not a consensus implementation. Security audit/current-policy rules remain mandatory even when a history data leg can read a projection.

## Evidence and Limits

Two SQLite files and explicit event delivery test rollback, committed replay, conflict/scope, lag fallback, duplicates/gaps, authority unavailability and restart persistence. A locked local breaker tests cooldown and a single probe per object. It is a sequential-result fixture, not a production breaker handling arbitrary late/in-flight result generations or distributed state. No model call, network replication, consensus, actual failover, collector/alert backend or measured objective is delivered.

## Operations and Revisit

Diagnose commit versus projection state, queue/pool/dependency waits, outbox age, gap watermarks, unknown effects and audit/policy availability. Fence old writers before promotion; reconcile before deleting evidence. Stage 8 may add quality/release versions and rollback while preserving operation identity and current access authority.
